description: OrbitWatch Ethiopia is a technology-focused team interested in software development, Earth observation, AI, and space exploration. We are developing OrbitWatch, an interactive platform that uses NASA-ISRO NISAR radar data to monitor and visualize changes on Earth's surface. Our goal is to make satellite observations accessible through interactive maps and change analysis, focusing on environmental challenges in Ethiopia. We welcome collaborators skilled in Python, GIS, remote sensing, AI/ML
summary: OrbitWatch Ethiopia is a satellite observation explorer which aims at helping users explore Earth observation data around the Hayli Gubbi study area in Ethiopia. The project combines Sentinel-2 optical imagery and NISAR synthetic aperture radar (SAR) amplitude quicklooks from two acquisition dates in an interactive dashboard. Users can explore the study area on a map, compare optical imagery with an opacity control and inspect radar observations side-by-side. OrbitWatch Ethiopia illustrates how different modalities of satellite observation can help to explore volcanic and environmental monitoring data by visualizing optical and radar data within a single interface. This prototype is an educational visualization tool; it does not perform validated SAR change detection, interferometric processing or ground-deformation measurements yet.
details:
OrbitWatch Ethiopia is an interactive satellite observation dashboard built to make Earth observation data easier to explore. It combines optical satellite imagery and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) amplitude quicklooks in one interface.

The dashboard uses Leaflet to display an interactive map and provides an opacity control for comparing two Sentinel-2 image dates. A separate radar section displays two NISAR-labelled SAR amplitude quicklooks side by side, allowing users to inspect differences in the visual appearance of the observations.

The project demonstrates how optical and radar observations can complement one another when exploring volcanic and environmental monitoring data. Its intended impact is to make satellite imagery more accessible to students, researchers, and people interested in Earth observation.

The frontend was developed using React, TypeScript, Vite, Leaflet, and CSS. OpenStreetMap provides the map baselayer. The radar quicklooks were generated from complex SAR data using Python-based processing and visualization.

The creative aspect is the integration of multiple satellite observation types into a simple, interactive dashboard. This is an early prototype: it does not yet perform calibrated change detection, interferometric analysis, or ground-deformation measurements.
